plan.title: Japan for Two in Spring: Route, Blossoms, Budget
plan.description: A first-timer's plan for a couple visiting Japan in spring: how many days to take, a Tokyo-Kyoto-Osaka route, and when the cherry blossoms are likely to peak. It also covers rail pass choices, realistic budget ranges and the etiquette that keeps a trip smooth.

beats.narration: Cherry blossoms peak for about one week. Miss it by a few days, and you may find bare branches or petals on the ground. So timing decides this whole trip.
beats.chapter: Timing the blossoms and choosing your days

beats.narration: Tokyo's thirty-year average puts first bloom on 24 March. For 2027, estimates suggest first bloom around 22 March, and full bloom around 30 March.
Kyoto is expected to open around 25 March, with full bloom around 3 April 2027. Normal is 26 March and 4 April. Osaka also peaks in early April.
Recent years show the range. In 2026, spring ran early, with Tokyo in full bloom on 28 March. In 2025, it was closer to normal.

props.alt: Blossoms in Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka

beats.narration: Official 2027 forecasts are not out yet. The first usually arrive in January, so stay flexible with bookings, and expect Kyoto's blossom week to be the busiest of the year.

props.label: When the first 2027 forecasts usually arrive

beats.narration: How many days? For a first couple's trip, plan ten to fourteen days. That gives time for Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka without rushing, and room to shift with the blossoms.

props.heading: Planning your window
items: Ten to fourteen days for two

beats.narration: Here is a simple route. Start in Tokyo, move on to Kyoto, and finish in Osaka. Osaka becomes your last base and your departure point.
beats.chapter: Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka: route and rail passes

beats.narration: One train line ties it together. The Tokaido Shinkansen links Tokyo, Nagoya, Kyoto and Osaka, so there is no need for complicated connections.
There is also something new. Since 1 October 2026, a private-cabin tier called Supreme Class sits above the Green Car on these trains. It is optional, so ordinary seats still work fine.
Now, the pass question. With only Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, add up single fares first. Tokyo to Kyoto is about 13,320 yen non-reserved, and Tokyo to Shin-Osaka is 13,870 yen.
Compare that with a nationwide seven-day pass at 50,000 yen. For this route, single tickets usually come out cheaper, and they let you ride the faster Nozomi.
Be careful with regional passes. The JR East Rail Pass and JR Tokyo Wide Pass cover eastern Japan around Tokyo. They do not reach Kyoto or Osaka.

props.heading: Regional passes
items: JR East Rail Pass: eastern Japan
JR Tokyo Wide Pass: eastern Japan

beats.narration: Two last tips. Book hotels early for blossom week, because it is the busiest week of the year. And in Kyoto, start your sightseeing at dawn to beat the crowds.
So what will it cost? Less than you might fear. A long weak yen has made ground costs roughly 25 to 30 percent cheaper for visitors paying in dollars, according to Wander Japan.

props.label: Cheaper ground costs for visitors paying in dollars

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.chapter: What it costs and how to behave

beats.narration: Per person, per day, without flights: budget is about 60 to 90 dollars. Mid-range is about 100 to 150. Luxury starts at 300 dollars and goes up.

props.title: Daily budget per person, no flights

beats.narration: Beds vary widely. A capsule is 2,000 to 5,000 yen a night. A Tokyo business hotel is 9,000 to 14,000. A ryokan, with dinner and breakfast, runs 15,000 to 45,000 yen or more per person.
For whole trips, Self Guide Japan shows a budget couple's ten days at about 2,160 dollars each, flights included. A mid-range fourteen days with two ryokan nights is about 3,720 dollars each.
Now the manners. Keep quiet on trains. In many areas, don't eat while walking. Take off your shoes where indicated. And carry your rubbish with you, because bins are rare.
Under the blossoms, don't shake branches or climb trees, and keep to the picnic areas. The trees are shared by everyone.

props.image_query: people picnic under cherry blossoms park

beats.narration: So the takeaway: plan ten to fourteen days, budget sensibly for each day, and be quiet, tidy and kind. Do that, and spring in Japan is yours.

props.text: Budget smart, travel quietly, leave no trace.
